section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a single study (Study 1) examining associations between positive body image measures and well-being in an online sample of 1148 U.K. adults. The study assessed multiple dimensions of positive body image (body appreciation, body image flexibility, body pride, body acceptance from others) and well-being (emotional, psychological, and social), controlling for age and BMI. Key findings indicate that body appreciation significantly predicted all dimensions of well-being, women scored lower on most body image measures than men, and BMI was negatively associated with all body image measures.
